# WO-2026-08-09-03 — Terra applies the household prose rulebook

## The defect, in one paragraph

**23 of 39 active household rules — 59% — cannot execute.** `actionableRules()`
(`services/asdair/skill/planner.js:952`) drops every `directive='info'` row and every row failing
`hasTarget()`; 20 of the 23 also have a NULL `match_term`. The planner's own comment concedes these
*"have never once fired."* The dead 59% is **not a random subset — it is precisely the judgement
layer.** Rule 31 *"Ariel Pods: pick the BEST VALUE by price-per-wash"* has been active since
2026-07-20 and never fired, which is why Warwick was asked to tap a button his own standing rule
already answered. Rule 36 *"if a multibuy gives ≥50% off the EXTRA item(s), buy up to the offer
quantity"* is `info` **and** targetless — doubly inert. Rule 37 (Sure pair rounding) — the same.
What survives is only `map` and `exclude`: *"toothpaste means Aquafresh"*, *"never buy banana Yazoo"*.

> **Warwick, verbatim:** *"there is no way to teach the system new rules and get it to learn if I
> keep having to tell it which aerial every bloody week!"*

**Larry's diagnosis, not Warwick's words:** the rules did not fail; the SHAPE they were forced into
failed. A judgement cannot be expressed as `map` or `exclude`, so every judgement was filed as `info`
and discarded. A model reading the same sentence in prose applies it with no schema at all.

## ⛔ The prohibition — read this before you design anything

**Do NOT invent an ever-growing deterministic mini-language for household shopping judgement.** This
is correction 3 of the sub-phase and it is the regrowth cap applied here. Adding `directive='value'`,
then `directive='rounding'`, then `directive='multibuy'` is the failure mode, not the fix — it is
BUILD-018 wearing a shopping apron.

**If your design adds a new directive type, a rule-expression grammar, a rules registry, or a
matcher DSL, you have taken the wrong branch.** The prose is the interface. Terra is the interpreter.

Deterministic selection may REMAIN where it already works — `map` and `exclude` are not to be torn
out. This is additive.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — The inert rules reach the reasoning consumer as prose.** Rules that
  `actionableRules()` currently discards are assembled into a prose rulebook and supplied to the
  reasoning consumer. Evidence: the exact assembled prose for the live corpus shape, pasted.
- **AC2 — Relevance, not the whole corpus.** Only rules plausibly relevant to the lines under
  consideration are sent. State your relevance method and its failure direction; **prefer
  over-inclusion to silent omission**, and say which you chose and why.
- **AC3 — A judgement rule changes a line.** Construct the three named cases — Rule 31
  (price-per-wash best value), Rule 36 (≥50%-off multibuy quantity), Rule 37 (pair rounding) — and
  demonstrate each changing a planned line that the deterministic path alone gets wrong. Executed
  output, pasted, all three.
- **AC4 — Attribution.** Every rulebook-driven change names the rule id that caused it. A correction
  nobody can trace to a rule is not acceptable — Warwick has to be able to ask *"why did it do that"*
  and get an answer.
- **AC5 — Uncertainty is spoken, never guessed and never silently parked.** This is correction 4 of
  the sub-phase, and it applies to an unclear OR self-contradicting prose rule exactly as it applies
  to an unmappable reply. When Terra cannot apply a rule confidently, that surfaces as a question —
  it does not silently fall through to the deterministic answer. Prove the unclear-rule path with an
  executed case.
- **AC6 — No new deterministic directive type.** Assert this in your return against your own diff.
  If you added one, AC6 FAILS and you say so plainly rather than arguing it was necessary.
- **AC7 — The pure interface is stated.** Wiring is excluded (see Sequencing). Your return must give
  Larry the exact function signature, inputs, outputs, and error/uncertainty behaviour the pipeline
  must call — precise enough to wire without reading your diff.

## Required evidence

- `cd services/asdair/skill && node --test` → **report the executed test COUNT and the pass/fail
  split, not the exit code alone.** A suite that silently ran zero cases is a green light for
  nothing; assert the count is non-zero and state it.
- **Mutation evidence for AC3.** Break your rulebook path on purpose — make it return no rules — and
  show the three cases go WRONG again. A control that no test can fail is not a control. Paste both
  directions.
- `bash scripts/secret-scan.sh --surface services/asdair/skill/planner.js services/asdair/skill/planner.test.js services/asdair/skill/ruleConsumption.test.js services/asdair/skill/rulebook.js services/asdair/skill/rulebook.test.js services/asdair/skill/README.md` → report exit code AND coverage. Exit 2 is NOT SCANNED, never a pass

## Inputs supplied

- `Deliverables/2026-08-04-build-015-asdair-wayfinder-plan.md` § SUB-PHASE B15-3 — the four defects
  D1–D4 and the five corrections. **Corrections 3, 4 and 5 are yours.**
- `services/asdair/skill/planner.js` — `actionableRules()` at line 952 and its own comment.
- `services/asdair/skill/ruleConsumption.test.js` — the existing consumption expectations.
- `services/asdair/interpret/groundedPrompt.js` — the existing grounded-prompt route. **Read it
  before inventing a second one**; if it already carries prose to the consumer, extend it rather
  than growing a parallel path, and say so.
- `services/asdair/db/007_rules_rotate_directive.sql`, `011_decisions_log_rule_notes_seed.sql` — the
  rule corpus shape and seeded notes.
- Rule corpus facts (from the live 2026-08-09 session, NOT re-queryable by you): 39 active, 23 inert,
  20 with NULL `match_term`; surviving types are `map` and `exclude`.

## Explicitly out of scope — report, never fix

- **Pipeline wiring.** `services/asdair/pipeline/deps.js`, `runPipeline.js` and `runtime.js` are NOT
  in your surface. Two other lanes are editing those files concurrently in other worktrees. Deliver
  a pure, callable interface; **Larry wires it during reconciliation.** Touching them collides.
- The free-text ingress and question surface (corrections 1 and 2) — Lane A owns those.
- The browser contract — Lane C owns that.
- Any schema or migration change to the rule corpus. Report it; Silas decides.
- Rewriting or re-classifying the household's actual rule rows. **The rules are Warwick's data. You
  make them executable; you do not edit them to suit your implementation.**

## Sequencing

1. **READ-BACK first** — the outcome as you understand it, your plan, what this order fails to
   settle, and what looks wrong. **Warwick has authorised execution and directed maximum speed, so
   you do NOT hold for Larry's acceptance:** state the read-back at the top of your return and
   continue straight into the work. If it surfaces something making the order genuinely unsafe or
   impossible, stop and return `REFUSE` with the reason.
2. Read `groundedPrompt.js` and `planner.js:952` before designing. Establish the real current route
   by reading it, never by assuming it.
3. Build the rulebook module and its tests. Keep `map`/`exclude` working.
4. Prove AC3 and AC5 with executed cases; mutation-test AC3 in both directions.
5. Commit onto `b15-3/terra-prose-rulebook` in your own worktree.
   **Git endpoint: commit only. NO push. NO PR. Do not touch `main`. Do not merge.**
6. Write your return to `Deliverables/2026-08-09-return-B15-R1-terra-prose-rulebook.md` in your
   worktree and commit it.

**Return structure:** READ-BACK · the current route as traced from source (file:line) · what you
built and why it is the smallest sufficient shape · executed evidence, pasted, including the
mutation run · AC1–AC7 each answered separately · the pure interface for Larry (AC7) · what is NOT
proven · residuals.

**Be honest about gaps.** A named gap is worth more to me than a confident claim. In particular: if
the judgement works in your tests but has never run in a real shop, say exactly that — it is the
difference between capability and completed automation, and this order does not and cannot close it.
